I am the office manager and I have been put in charge of organizing our Corporate Wellness Week. I have an event brief PDF in my workspace called Event_Brief.pdf that has all the details about the event including dates, attendee count, budget, and dietary requirements. Please start by reading through that document carefully.

We need to plan daily menus for the entire week. Each day needs one breakfast recipe and one lunch recipe. I would like you to search through our recipe catalog and find suitable options. We need at least 2 vegetarian options spread across the week, and ideally the meals should be reasonable in terms of nutrition. There is also a planning guide called guide.md in the workspace that explains our cost calculation approach.

Before finalizing the menu, please also check our company health and wellness portal at http://localhost:30180 to review the dietary guidelines and any allergen information we need to be aware of. The portal has a guidelines page with recommended daily nutritional values we should try to stay within.

Once you have selected the recipes and gathered all the information, create an Excel file called Wellness_Menu_Plan.xlsx with three sheets. This must be a single workbook containing all three sheets (Daily Menu, Ingredient Summary, and Budget Overview) produced together as one coherent file. The first sheet should be called Daily Menu and should list out each day from Monday through Friday, sorted by day, with columns for Day, Meal_Type (Breakfast or Lunch), Recipe_Name, Servings (which is 50 for all meals since we have 50 attendees), Ingredient_Count (the number of unique food ingredients in that recipe), Estimated_Cost (calculated as ingredient count times $0.50 times 50 people, rounded to 2 decimal places), and Is_Vegetarian (Yes or No). That gives us 10 rows total, two meals per day.

The second sheet should be called Ingredient Summary and should aggregate all ingredients across every recipe. List each ingredient alphabetically with columns Ingredient_Name, Total_Quantity (just put 1 for each occurrence since quantities vary), Unit (use "unit" as default), Times_Used (how many recipes use that ingredient), and Total_Cost (times used times $0.50 times 50, rounded to 2 decimal places).

The third sheet should be called Budget Overview with two columns Label and Value. Include rows for Total_Budget ($2000), Total_Estimated_Cost (sum of all daily costs from the Daily Menu sheet), Budget_Remaining (total budget minus estimated cost), Avg_Cost_Per_Day (total estimated cost divided by 5), Avg_Cost_Per_Meal (total estimated cost divided by 10), and Days_Over_Budget (count of days where the combined breakfast plus lunch cost exceeds $400).

Note: write every numeric value (Servings, Ingredient_Count, Estimated_Cost, Total_Quantity, Times_Used, Total_Cost, and all Budget Overview values) as a literal number in the cell. Do not write Excel formulas (e.g., do not use "=A2*0.5*50" — instead compute the number and enter it directly).

After the Excel is done, I need you to schedule 5 calendar events for meal prep sessions, one for each day of the wellness week. They should be from 7:00 AM to 8:00 AM on March 16, 17, 18, 19, and 20, 2026. Title each one "Wellness Week Meal Prep - [Day]" where Day is Monday through Friday respectively. Specify the times in UTC using ISO-8601 format without a timezone offset, e.g. start 2026-03-16T07:00:00 and end 2026-03-16T08:00:00.

Finally, send two emails. The first one goes to catering_vendor@company.com with subject "Wellness Week Ingredient Order" and the body should include a summary list of all unique ingredients needed across all recipes and the total estimated cost. The second email goes to wellness_committee@company.com with subject "Wellness Week Menu Plan" and the body should include an overview of the daily menu showing which recipes are planned for each day along with the total budget summary.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly as the main agent without dispatching any sub-agents. Read Event_Brief.pdf with the authorized PDF read tools and guide.md, and fetch the health-portal landing and dietary-guidelines pages in one native-parallel batch, freezing the event constraints (date, headcount, budget, dietary rules) before any recipe work. Browse the howtocook database directly, select the required dishes per the brief, and join them to the portal nutrition rules to compute per-person portions and totals with calculation notes. Then, in one pass per deliverable: write the catering workbook with the exact sheets/headers and literal values (one bulk write per sheet plus one final read-back); create each calendar event exactly once from the frozen schedule with explicit timezones (search exact summaries first, create only missing, read IDs back); and send the summary email exactly once to the brief-defined recipient/subject (paginate Sent search first, read the retained message back). Reconcile workbook, events and email against the frozen menu, then call claim_done; do not add a separate verification phase.

You are a planning sub-agent. Decompose the following task into ordered subtasks. Do NOT execute the task — only produce a plan.

CONTEXT:
- Workspace directory: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-fetch-howtocook-catering-excel-gcal-email/workspace
- The user is an office manager organizing a Corporate Wellness Week. In the workspace there is an event brief PDF (Event_Brief.pdf) with event details (dates, attendee count, budget, dietary requirements) and a planning guide (guide.md) explaining cost calculation approach.
- There is a recipe catalog accessible via the `mcp__howtocook` MCP server (functions like mcp_howtocook_getAllRecipes, mcp_howtocook_getRecipeById, mcp_howtocook_getRecipesByCategory, mcp_howtocook_recommendMeals, mcp_howtocook_whatToEat).
- There is a company health/wellness portal at http://localhost:30180 with a guidelines page containing recommended daily nutritional values and allergen info (fetch via mcp__fetch tools).

TASK GOALS (from user):
1. Read Event_Brief.pdf and guide.md carefully (both in the workspace).
2. Plan daily menus for the whole week (Monday–Friday): each day needs 1 breakfast recipe + 1 lunch recipe (10 meals total). Need at least 2 vegetarian options across the week; meals should be reasonable nutritionally.
3. Check the wellness portal at http://localhost:30180 for dietary guidelines and allergen info before finalizing the menu.
4. Create Excel file Wellness_Menu_Plan.xlsx with exactly 3 sheets in one workbook:
   - Sheet "Daily Menu": rows for Monday–Friday, 2 rows per day (10 total), sorted by day, columns: Day, Meal_Type (Breakfast/Lunch), Recipe_Name, Servings (=50 for all), Ingredient_Count (number of unique food ingredients in recipe), Estimated_Cost (= ingredient count * $0.50 * 50, rounded to 2 decimals), Is_Vegetarian (Yes/No).
   - Sheet "Ingredient Summary": aggregate all ingredients across every recipe, alphabetical, columns: Ingredient_Name, Total_Quantity (literal 1 per occurrence), Unit ("unit" default), Times_Used (how many recipes use that ingredient), Total_Cost (Times_Used * $0.50 * 50, rounded to 2 decimals).
   - Sheet "Budget Overview": two columns Label and Value, rows: Total_Budget (2000), Total_Estimated_Cost (sum of Daily Menu costs), Budget_Remaining, Avg_Cost_Per_Day (total/5), Avg_Cost_Per_Meal (total/10), Days_Over_Budget (count of days where combined breakfast+lunch cost > $400).
   - IMPORTANT: all numeric values must be written as literal numbers (no Excel formulas).
5. Schedule 5 calendar events (Google Calendar): "Wellness Week Meal Prep - Monday/Friday" on March 16–20, 2026, 07:00–08:00 UTC, ISO-8601 without timezone offset (e.g. 2026-03-16T07:00:00 to 2026-03-16T08:00:00).
6. Send 2 emails:
   - To catering_vendor@company.com, subject "Wellness Week Ingredient Order": body with summary list of all unique ingredients across all recipes + total estimated cost.
   - To wellness_committee@company.com, subject "Wellness Week Menu Plan": body with daily menu overview (recipes per day) + total budget summary.

WHAT YOU SHOULD DO:
- Inspect the workspace (list files, read Event_Brief.pdf if possible — it may be a PDF; note whether text extraction is feasible or whether the main agent needs to handle it — and read guide.md) to ground the plan in actual file contents.
- Optionally probe the recipe catalog and the portal (read-only) to understand data shapes, but keep it light — the plan mainly needs to specify ordered subtasks.
- Produce a plan with ordered subtasks. For each subtask specify:
  - dispatch decision: `self` (main agent), `explore`, or `coder`
  - whether it is independent (parallelizable) or must wait for another subtask's output
- Include a verification strategy per subtask (how to check correctness, e.g. Excel has 3 sheets with exact names, calendar has 5 events, emails sent).

DELIVERABLE: Return a concise ordered subtask list with dispatch decisions, dependencies, and acceptance criteria for each. Note any risks (e.g. PDF extraction issues, recipe data shapes, portal structure).
Plan wellness week task

You are a coder sub-agent. Your task: extract the text content from the PDF file at:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-fetch-howtocook-catering-excel-gcal-email/workspace/Event_Brief.pdf

BACKGROUND: The file is a 2-page ReportLab-generated PDF. The plan agent found its streams are ASCII85 + Flate compressed, so it may NOT be readable via plain text tools. You have terminal access (python, etc.) and filesystem access within the workspace.

DO THIS:
1. Use the terminal to run Python in the workspace directory (/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-fetch-howtocook-catering-excel-gcal-email/workspace). First try any installed PDF library (pypdf, PyPDF2, pdfplumber, fitz/PyMuPDF). If none works, implement a stdlib-only extractor: read the PDF bytes, locate the stream objects, base64.a85decode them, zlib.decompress them, and parse the text-showing operators (Tj, TJ, etc.) to recover the text.
2. Save the extracted plain text to a file in the workspace: Event_Brief_extracted.txt
3. Print the full extracted text in your final report so the main agent can see it verbatim.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Work only inside the workspace directory given above.
- Do not modify Event_Brief.pdf itself.

DELIVERABLE / ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Event_Brief_extracted.txt exists in the workspace with legible extracted text.
- Your report must include the FULL extracted text verbatim, plus a short bullet list of the key facts you can confirm from it: event dates, attendee count, total budget, dietary requirements/allergens, vegetarian requirements, and anything about meals (breakfast/lunch), cost rules, or vendor emails if present.
- If extraction is impossible with all methods, report exactly what error occurred and what the raw streams look like (first ~500 chars). Do NOT fabricate content.
Extract Event_Brief.pdf text

You are an explore sub-agent (read-only). Your task: map out the recipe catalog exposed by the `mcp__howtocook` MCP server so the main agent can pick 10 recipes (5 breakfasts + 5 lunches) for a Corporate Wellness Week (Mon–Fri, 50 attendees).

TOOLS YOU HAVE: mcp__howtocook__mcp_howtocook_getAllRecipes, mcp_howtocook_getRecipeById (query by name or id, fuzzy match), mcp_howtocook_getRecipesByCategory (categories: 水产, 早餐, 调料, 甜品, 饮品, 荤菜, 半成品加工, 汤, 主食, 素菜), mcp_howtocook_recommendMeals, mcp_howtocook_whatToEat. All read-only. Do NOT create/update anything.

KNOWN DATA SHAPES (from prior recon): getAllRecipes returns only name+description (no ingredients). Full data — including `ingredients[]` with fields like name/text_quantity/quantity/unit, and a category field — comes from getRecipeById / getRecipesByCategory. Ingredient lists contain NOISE: kitchen tools (微波炉/锅/漏勺/蒸架/碗/刀 etc.), optional items ("糖（可选）", "可根据口味选择增加" etc.), duplicated entries (bare + quantified versions, e.g. 鸡蛋 vs 鸡蛋两个 vs 🥚鸡蛋), "--" placeholders, truncated names. Some recipes have empty ingredients (e.g. 温泉蛋). Recipe names may be Chinese or English.

DO THIS:
1. Call mcp_howtocook_getAllRecipes to see the full catalog.
2. Call mcp_howtocook_getRecipesByCategory for at least: 早餐 (breakfast candidates), 素菜 (vegetarian lunch candidates), 荤菜, 主食, 汤 (lunch candidates). For each category, list the recipes.
3. For the most promising ~20-25 recipes (aim for a good mix: several 早餐 options, several 素菜, several 荤菜/主食/汤), call mcp_howtocook_getRecipeById to get full details including ingredient lists.
4. For each recipe you detail, record: recipe name (exact, as returned), category, full raw ingredient list, and a CLEANED unique ingredient list. Cleaning rule (apply consistently): drop kitchen tools/equipment; drop items marked optional; drop "--" placeholders; dedupe within a recipe (e.g. 鸡蛋 vs 鸡蛋两个 → one entry 鸡蛋); canonicalize obvious duplicates; decide ONCE whether to count 水/water as an ingredient (recommend: exclude it as a non-purchased staple, but state your decision explicitly). Note recipes whose ingredient list is empty/trivial — flag them as unusable.
5. Assess vegetarian status: 素菜 category recipes are vegetarian; note any breakfast/主食/汤 recipes that appear meat/fish/egg-free (report facts as listed in the data, e.g. whether ingredients contain 肉/鱼/虾/蛋 etc.).

DELIVERABLE: A structured report containing:
- The full category listings you retrieved (recipe names per category).
- A candidate table with columns: Recipe_Name | Category | Vegetarian (Yes/No/Unknown) | Cleaned unique ingredient list (food items only) | Raw ingredient count vs cleaned count.
- Your stated cleaning rules and the water decision.
- Explicitly list any recipes that contain peanuts (花生) or shellfish (虾/蟹/贝/蛤/蚝 etc.) — the wellness portal says these allergens must be avoided.
- Note any recipes with empty/trivial ingredient lists (unusable).
Keep the report organized and complete — the main agent will select the final 10 recipes from your table without re-querying.
Explore recipe catalog
